<reason>A won by forcing a clean dilemma: the duty either restates already-criminal threats as a deeper-pocket claim, or it reaches still-lawful coordination that looks like protest, reporting, and swarming, where volume plus hindsight make over-removal the rational response. B’s complementary-duty and specified-precautions case was coherent, but never produced a non-criminal class identifiable in real time without later knowledge of harm, nor showed why a post-injury “when warranted” inquiry would beat throttling organized anger.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: live-location targeting is either already stalking or ordinary public reporting, and a safe harbor still litigating credibility/proportion/“when warranted” after injury is not cheaper than making the swarm vanish.</best_rebuttal>
